subject: BlueHarbor PoC — connectivity options and recommended next steps

Subject: RedWood private PoC — connectivity options and constraints

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. BlueHarbor is ready to spin up a short PoC for Redwood Private (VPC deployment) but our security and network teams need to agree on how to connect our on-prem environment to Redwood's VPCs.

High-level constraints from our side:
- We cannot expose any management plane endpoints to public internet.
- All traffic must be TLS+mutual-auth and originate from fixed egress IPs where possible.
- Cross-region latency must be under 50ms for inference pipelines that span multi-site backends.

Attached is our current network diagram (BH_Network_Diagram_v2.pdf). Can you outline pros/cons for the three patterns we discussed (VPC peering, PrivateLink, site-to-site VPN) and recommend a primary + fallback pattern? Also, rough cost/order-of-magnitude and any configuration gotchas to call out.

Can we get a short write-up by Wednesday so our NetOps can review before the architecture sync?

Appreciate it —
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director of Partnerships, BlueHarbor Health

Subject: Re: RedWood private PoC — connectivity options and constraints

Aisha —

Thanks for the diagram and constraints. Looping in Karthik and Soojin from our infra/networks team; I pulled together a concise comparison below and an initial recommendation. Attaching a short checklist for the PoC (redwood-connection-checklist.md) and a first-pass cost sheet.

Summary comparison (very high level):

1) VPC Peering
- Pros: Lowest latency (L3), simple route tables, native AWS path; no NLB required.
- Cons: No cross-account private DNS by default; peering does not scale well for many VPCs (mesh complexity); not supported across some regions/providers without transit.
- Operational: Requires careful CIDR planning and route propagation. Useful when both sides control VPCs and want predictable, low-latency data plane.

2) AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints)
- Pros: Strong isolation (only exposed services), no route table changes for consumer; supports cross-account access securely; DNS-based access patterns (svc.<zone>.aws).
- Cons: Higher per-endpoint cost; slightly higher latency than peering due to ENI termination; requires NLB or service behind it on provider side.
- Operational: Great for exposing a small set of controlled services (API endpoints) to consumer VPCs without full VPC visibility.

3) Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
- Pros: Works to on-prem directly, easy to set up for PoC; low up-front config, supports static egress IPs; can be used as a fallback path.
- Cons: Higher and variable latency; throughput limited by tunnels; not ideal for high-throughput, low-latency inference traffic.
- Operational: Need to manage tunnel endpoints, BGP if used, and key rotations.

Recommendation (primary + fallback):
- Primary: VPC Peering for compute-heavy inference (dedicated/hosted collocated VPCs) when low latency is required and both VPCs are under controlled accounts/regions.
- Fallback/Service exposure: PrivateLink for control plane APIs (model management, metrics ingestion) where we want tight surface area and API-level access without full VPC access.
- On-prem direct: Use Site-to-Site VPN only as a temporary PoC or backup for non-latency-sensitive ingestion (batch ops, admin consoles).

Callouts / gotchas:
- Egress IP expectations: If BlueHarbor needs fixed egress IPs for allowlists, we must NAT through a set of dedicated NAT gateways or use a fixed Elastic IP on a managed NLB + egress proxy.
- Cross-region traffic: Peering across regions can be done but varies by cloud; measure RTT in a small test — we can instrument this during PoC.
- DNS: PrivateLink will require split-horizon DNS or explicit endpoint hostnames; peering requires shared route53 private hosted zones or conditional forwarding.
- Throughput: If inference involves >1Gbps sustained, PrivateLink data plane costs and per-ENI throughput need validation.

Next steps I propose:
- We run a 48hr latency/throughput PoC with a small model to compare peering vs PrivateLink for your most latency-sensitive endpoint. Redwood will provision a test VPC and coordinate IP/CIDR.
- Karthik can share a step-by-step runbook (I copied him).

I can get a slightly expanded doc by COB Wednesday. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RedWood private PoC — connectivity options and constraints

Aisha / team —

Adding a more tactical checklist and a couple of configuration notes from NetOps perspective:

PoC checklist (expanded):
- Agree on CIDR ranges for test VPCs and on-prem segments (avoid overlap).
- Decide on routing method: static routes for small PoC or BGP over VPN for dynamic.
- For peering: confirm we can create cross-account peering and update route tables on both sides. Provide peering request workflow id to us.
- For PrivateLink: we will front Redwood service with an NLB in our provider account; you will create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC. Provide approved security group egress for the ENIs.
- For VPN: exchange public IPs for your firewall, pre-shared key, and whether you'll use BGP.

Performance measurement plan:
- We will deploy a small inference service and run 1) p99 latency tests with 0/16/64 token prompts and 2) sustained throughput run at target QPS.
- Instrumentation: packet captures (pcap) for first 30 minutes, application metrics (RTT, cert handshake time), and CloudWatch/Datadog dashboards.

Security notes:
- Mutual TLS termination: Redwood supports mTLS to our API endpoints; we recommend mTLS for PrivateLink traffic and a client cert overlay for peering.
- Audit logs: we will enable flow logs for the peering connection and provide S3 access for your auditors for the PoC window.

I'll be available for the architecture sync — happy to walk through configuration snippets.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Let's plan the 48hr PoC next week: can Redwood provision the test VPC by Monday morning? Also, Michael will share our firewall public IPs so we can test VPN as a fallback.

Aisha

We created the test VPC (redwood-poctest-us-west-2) and the PrivateLink service for the model-control API. I've attached a short runbook with commands and the NLB details. Key notes:

- Test VPC CIDR: 10.66.16.0/20 (Please confirm this doesn't overlap with your on-prem ranges).
- PrivateLink DNS: service will be available at model-control.us-west-2.redwood.internal; you can create an Interface Endpoint with that hostname.
- Latency baseline (initial internal checks): peering-equivalent RTT ~12ms, PrivateLink ~18–22ms for the same region under light load. We'll run the official p99 measurements during the PoC.

Next actions for BlueHarbor:
- Confirm CIDR non-overlap and share firewall public IPs for VPN fallback.
- Schedule the architecture sync (30 min) — propose Monday 10:00am PT.
